description: TNA (Time & Action) spreadsheet extraction. A workbook describes garment production orders for one or more buyers. Each Product Line Item (PLI) = one style + color combination being ordered, with a set of production milestones (stages). PLIs appear in three possible layouts: (a) ROW-PER-PLI — each row is one PLI with stage columns to the right; (b) SHEET-IS-PLI — the entire sheet describes one PLI as key/value pairs scattered around it; (c) SECTION-PER-PLI — multiple PLIs stacked vertically on one sheet, each as a multi-row section. Output the same flat shape regardless of layout: a list of PLI objects with stages nested inside each PLI. Two PLIs may legitimately share the same io_number — do NOT deduplicate. Copy cell content verbatim: do not split one cell across multiple fields, do not concatenate multiple cells into one field, do not strip leading zeros or reformat. If a field is not present in the workbook, leave it null. Skip helper sheets named 'Help', 'Master', 'Codes', 'Lookups', 'Legend', cover/title pages, and pure summary sheets.

plis.description: Every PLI found in the workbook, in document order. A PLI is valid if you can find at least one identifier — io_number is the most reliable (almost every TNA has it under some label); style_code+color_code or quantity may serve as a fallback identifier when io_number is absent. Do NOT emit a PLI with no identifiers at all.

items.description: One PLI. Populate fields you can verify from the workbook; leave the rest null. Faithful extraction: copy values verbatim from the source cell.

io_number.description: Primary per-row order identifier — usually a short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the buyer's order. The most reliable PLI identifier; nearly every TNA workbook contains it under some label. Copy verbatim. If a 'Buyer PO' column is the primary per-row identifier, map it here (not to metadata.buyer_po_no). Use metadata.buyer_po_no only when a separate io_number-style column also exists.

style_code.description: Style identifier — a short alphanumeric code for the garment style. May be absent. Copy verbatim. If a 'STYLE' column contains a combined code+name like '890162 TAVIRA_2 522148' or 'STYLE_NAME / STYLE-CODE', extract the entire cell value as style_code. If the cell is a pure descriptive name like 'D-T-SHIRT 3/4', put it in style_name instead.

style_name.description: Descriptive style name (e.g. 'D-T-SHIRT 3/4', 'POLO LS', 'CARGO PANT'). Use when the cell holds words rather than a code. Copy verbatim.

color_code.description: Color identifier — usually a short alphanumeric color code. May be absent. Copy verbatim.

color_name.description: Descriptive color name (e.g. 'NAVY', 'BLACK', 'BURGUNDY 432'). Use when the cell value is a name rather than a code.

fabric_code.description: Fabric identifier — an alphanumeric code OR a fabric description like '100% COTTON 30S'. May be absent. Copy verbatim. If the source column is named 'Fabric Quality', 'Material Quality', 'Fabric Type', or 'Fabric Description', map the value here, NOT to metadata. Every column that holds a fabric description should populate this field.

quantity.description: Total order quantity in units (pieces). Integer. This is the canonical 'how many pieces are being ordered' field; every column that holds an order/plan/required quantity maps here, NOT to metadata.order_quantity or metadata.plan_quantity. Round non-integer numeric cells (e.g. 1500.0) to integer; if the cell shows 'PO' or non-numeric text, leave null. Can serve as a secondary identifier when style/color codes are absent.

delivery_date.description: Promised delivery / ex-factory / ETD date for the order. The canonical 'when does this PLI ship' field; every column whose header looks like 'Delivery Date', 'Ex Factory Date', 'ETD', 'ETD Ex Factory as per P.O', or 'Shipment Date' maps here, NOT to metadata.ex_factory_date or metadata.etd_ex_factory. Output YYYY-MM-DD. Input formats vary: DD-MMM-YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, DD.MM.YYYY are common. If the cell value isn't a parseable date, leave null.
x-alternativeNames: Etd Ex factory as per P.O

metadata.description: Additional PLI-level fields that don't fit the canonical PLI fields above. Populate only keys you find in the workbook; leave the rest null. These are PLI-level (apply to the whole PLI), not stage-level. Do NOT duplicate canonical PLI fields here — quantity, delivery_date, fabric_code, etc. always go in their top-level PLI field.

buyer_po_no.description: Buyer's PO number, ONLY when a separate io_number-style column also exists. If buyer-PO is the primary per-row identifier, it goes in io_number instead.

article_no.description: Article number, if separate from style_code.

balance_qty.description: Balance quantity remaining to ship, if separate from order quantity.

order_receipt_date.description: Date the order was received by the factory.

sample_dispatch.description: Date a sample was dispatched. This is an admin/lifecycle date, not a production-stage date.

stages.description: Production milestones for this PLI. Layouts vary: (a) WIDE COLUMNS — one column per stage; (b) WIDE COLUMNS WITH SUB-COLUMNS — each stage spans Plan/Actual/Approved-Qty sub-columns; (c) BAND-SEPARATED — stages stacked vertically inside the PLI section, each band = header row + child rows; (d) TALL ROWS — one row per stage. Output the same flat shape regardless. Two stages MAY share a name (e.g. two 'Sewing' bands for different sub-orders) — do not deduplicate.

items.description: One production milestone. Map the spreadsheet's header to a canonical stage name. Never emit a stage whose name matches a PLI field — 'delivery_date', 'ex_factory_date', 'fabric_code' are PLI fields, not stages; skip those columns when iterating stages.

name.description: Canonical stage name in snake_case. Choose the closest match from this fixed list: fabric, lab_dip_send, lab_dip_approval, fit_send, fit_approval, art_work_send, art_work_approval, in_house_fabric_send, in_house_fabric_approval, pre_production_send, pre_production_approval, first_pattern, garment_pattern, planned_completion_date, size_set, lot_card, cutting, feeding, sewing, sewing_start, sewing_end, final_inspection, printing, embroidery, washing, finishing, packing, ex_factory, trims_inhouse. If a header looks like a PLI field (e.g. 'Delivery Date', 'Ex Factory Date as per P.O') and not a production milestone, skip it — do NOT emit it as a stage. Examples: 'Ex Factory Shipment' → ex_factory; 'Sewing Start' → sewing_start; 'Final Inspection' / 'FI' → final_inspection; 'Trims Inhouse' → trims_inhouse.

planned_date.description: The planned / scheduled / target date for this stage. In multi-column layouts this is usually under a 'Plan' or 'Planned Date' sub-column. In single-date layouts it's the only date cell associated with the stage. Output YYYY-MM-DD.

actual_date.description: The actual completion / approval / receipt date of this stage. Null if not yet completed.

quantity.description: Stage-level quantity if recorded (e.g. approved qty for a lab dip, cut qty, sewn qty, shipped qty). Null if not present.

remarks.description: Free-text comments / notes / status for this stage (e.g. 'Pending approval', 'Delayed 3 days', 'Lab dip rejected, re-send').

section.description: If stages are organised into sections/groups (e.g. 'Fabric & Trims', 'Sample Approval', 'Production', 'Cutting & Sewing', 'Finishing & Packing'), record the section header here. Null if no sectioning is used.

sheet.description: Name of the sheet this PLI was extracted from. Useful in multi-sheet workbooks, especially SHEET-IS-PLI layouts where each sheet represents one PLI.
